public_rationale: The support condition asks for tests from about March to June 2026 that show frontier models still giving confident wrong answers at substantial rates. On 2026-04-23, Artificial Analysis, an independent benchmark operator, reported hallucination rates on its AA-Omniscience knowledge benchmark (e1). This rate measures how often a model gives a wrong answer instead of declining when it does not answer correctly. It was 86% for GPT-5.5 (xhigh), 50% for Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview and 36% for Claude Opus 4.7 (max) (e1). The same source said GPT-5.5's gain over GPT-5.4 came mostly from knowledge, with a modest improvement in hallucination (e1). A secondary summary published 2026-04-29 reports that OpenAI's system card found GPT-5.5's claims 23% more likely to be correct than GPT-5.4's, with factual errors 3% less often (e2). Those gains are relative to the previous model. They do not report near-zero error rates. The support condition is met. The contradiction condition, near-zero error rates on standard factuality benchmarks, is not met by any item in the packet.
limitations: AA-Omniscience uses hard knowledge questions and counts only non-correct answers. It does not show error rates on everyday tasks.
'Reliability' is broader than factuality. This assessment uses hallucination and factual-error measures only.
The system-card figures come from a secondary summary, not the system card itself.
There is no agreed threshold for when hallucination counts as solved.
